examples.ko: 이 나무는 가지가 굵직굵직해서 튼튼해 보여요.
examples.en: This tree has thick branches, so it looks sturdy.
Big, major incidents happened one after another this year.
I cut the potatoes into chunky pieces and put them in the stew.

examples.ko: 굵직굵직했던 경기들이 이번 달에 몰려 있어요.
examples.en: The major games are packed into this month.
His finger joints are thick and sturdy.

examples.ko: 굵직굵직하고 단단한 기둥이 지붕을 받치고 있어요.
examples.en: Thick, solid pillars are holding up the roof.

explain: '굵다'와 달리 하나가 아니라 여러 개가 다 굵직할 때 많이 써요. 음식 재료를 큼직하게 썰 때도 쓰고, '굵직굵직한 사건', '굵직굵직한 작품'처럼 중요하고 큰 일이 여러 개일 때도 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '굵다', it is often used when several things are all thick. It is used for chunky-cut ingredients, and also for several big, important things, as in '굵직굵직한 사건' (major incidents) or '굵직굵직한 작품' (major works).

examples.en: This problem needs a multifaceted approach.
The teacher evaluates students from multiple perspectives.

examples.ko: 다면적 분석을 해야 정확한 결과가 나와요.
examples.en: You need a multifaceted analysis to get accurate results.

examples.ko: 그는 다면적 성격을 가진 사람이라 알기 어려워요.
examples.en: He has a many-sided personality, so he's hard to figure out.

examples.ko: 회사는 직원을 다면적 평가 방식으로 심사해요.
examples.en: The company reviews employees through a multi-angle evaluation method.

examples.ko: 그 사건에는 다면적 원인이 얽혀 있어요.
examples.en: Many different causes are tangled up in that incident.

explain: '다면적 평가', '다면적 접근', '다면적 분석'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 서술어로 말할 때는 '다면적이다'나 '다면적인'으로도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 '다각적'은 여러 방향에서 본다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is placed before a noun, as in '다면적 평가', '다면적 접근' and '다면적 분석'. As a predicate you can also say '다면적이다' or '다면적인'. The similar '다각적' has a stronger feeling of looking from several directions.

examples.ko: 정수리 쪽 머리카락이 듬성듬성 나 있어요.
examples.en: The hair on the crown of my head is growing thinly.
I scattered lettuce seeds sparsely in the garden plot.
The students are sitting spread out in the classroom.
His beard is patchy, so he looks untidy.
I walked along a road with patches of snow here and there.

examples.ko: 옷에 흰 털이 듬성듬성 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There are white hairs stuck here and there on your clothes.

explain: 사이가 성기게 드문드문 있는 모양을 말해요. 반대는 '빽빽이', '촘촘히'예요. '띄엄띄엄'은 시간 간격에도 쓰지만 '듬성듬성'은 머리카락·씨앗·사람처럼 공간에서 드물게 있을 때 써요.
explain_en: It describes things placed or growing far apart with gaps between them. Its opposites are '빽빽이' and '촘촘히' (densely). '띄엄띄엄' can also describe time intervals, but '듬성듬성' is for things sparse in space, like hair, seeds or people.

examples.en: A can is shaped like a cylinder.
I solved a problem about finding the volume of a cylinder.
A cylinder has round top and bottom faces.
This container looks like a cylinder.
If you lay a cylinder on its side, it rolls easily.
In math class, we made a cylinder out of paper.

explain: 수학 시간에 주로 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '통 모양'이라고 말하기도 해요. 같이 배우는 도형으로 '원뿔', '각기둥'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly a math-class word; in daily life people may say '통 모양' (tube shape). Shapes studied alongside it include '원뿔' (cone) and '각기둥' (prism).

examples.ko: 졸업식 날 학생들은 모두 검은 옷 일색이었어요.
examples.en: On graduation day the students were all in black.

examples.ko: 이 동네 가게는 치킨집 일색이라 다른 음식이 그리워요.
examples.en: The shops in this neighborhood are all chicken places, so I miss other food.
The meeting room was all men, so it felt a little awkward.

examples.ko: 응원 온 사람들이 붉은색 일색으로 입고 왔어요.
examples.en: The people who came to cheer all wore red.

examples.ko: 비슷한 건물 일색인 거리를 걷다 보니 지루해졌어요.
examples.en: Walking along the street of nothing but similar buildings got boring.
These days TV is all about food.

explain: '흰색 일색', '남자 일색'처럼 앞에 색이나 사람, 사물을 붙여서 한 가지로만 채워진 모습을 말해요. '일색이다'처럼 서술어로도 쓰고, 다양하지 않다는 느낌이 들 때가 많아요.
explain_en: You attach a color, a type of person or a thing before it, as in '흰색 일색' or '남자 일색', to say something is filled with just one kind. It can also be used as a predicate, '일색이다', and it often suggests a lack of variety.

en: to be tiny; to be fine

examples.en: The writing is so tiny that it is hard to read.
There were lots of little tasks, so I was busy again today.
I picked up tiny shells at the beach.
Please chop the onion finely and add it.
The small worries I had are nothing now.
Even if the expenses are small, they add up to a lot.

explain: '작다'와 달리 작은 것들이 여럿 모여 있을 때 어울려요. '자잘한 글씨, 자잘한 일'처럼 쓰고, 일에 쓰면 '사소한'에 가까워요. 비슷한 말로 '자질구레하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike '작다', it fits when many small things are gathered together, as in '자잘한 글씨' or '자잘한 일'. Used for tasks it means 'trivial'. A similar word is '자질구레하다'.
